name: Rheon Systems CorpSec Field Loadout MK-6
description:
Head-to-toe tactical rig issued to mid-tier CorpSec units. Matte-black segmented TacShell torso armor over a moisture-wicking graphene underlayer, ballistic-rated ceramic shoulder pauldrons, and articulated knee-strike greaves. Helmet is a low-profile carbon composite with integrated HUD visor and neural uplink port at the occipital ridge. Gloves are cut-resistant syntex with haptic feedback nodes at the fingertips.

Boots are steel-shank, oil-resistant, with mag-lock heel capability. All panels connect via quick-release buckles for field maintenance. The entire kit ships in a compressed carry-bag and assembles in under four minutes. Standard colorway is gunmetal with amber corponation stripe.
functionality: Full ballistic protection to Class 3, integrated neural HUD uplink, mag-lock boot heel for surface adhesion, quick-release panel system for field repair, thermal signature dampening on torso.
what_it_says: You are a sanctioned instrument of force — credentialed, equipped, and expendable.
story_hooks: A unit's loadout serial number traces back to a black-site requisition that officially never happened.
The HUD uplink has a firmware backdoor — someone is watching through every officer's visor.
A disgraced CorpSec officer still has her full kit; no one came to collect it after she was burned.
